# Stage 2.1: Initial Explorations of the Dataset.

## About

### Dataset
The datasets I am exploring are [Flock Camera's Per State](https://flockscanner.com/flock-camera-map/), and [2024 Election Results Data](https://digitalcommons.bucknell.edu/election_data/2/).  It is stored in the `_data` folder.

### Research Question
My initial research question is pretty vague -- _"Is there an association between the 2024 Election Results and the support of Flock Cameras?"_ I am not too sure if this is where I want to go with this or if there is something more I can explore. 

## First question: which states? 
I first want to know where the flock cameras are showing up. Which states have the most flock cameras? 

```{python}
import pandas as pd
from pyprojroot import here # this helps us navigate tricky path stuff between local runs and quarto builds

# Load the data using here() with the path from the project root
file_path_state = here("projects/leah/_data/flockperstate.csv")
per_state_df = pd.read_csv(file_path_state, sep=',')  
# removing the commas and making the column numeric 
per_state_df["Flock Cameras"] = pd.to_numeric(per_state_df["Flock Cameras"].str.replace(",", ""))

# sort the states in to descending order based on the flock camera number  
sorted = per_state_df.sort_values(by=["Flock Cameras"], ascending=False)

print(sorted.head(5))

```

Now I know the top five states with the most flock cameras. I can now focus my attention on these states in particular. 

## Second Question: where?
Before I move on with this line, I want to figure out where the cameras are placed within the states. Specifically what kind of establishments have the cameras on their property. For this, I am going to explore the private operators of Flock cameras. Who invests in flock cameras, meaning where within the states/cities are they found? 

```{python}
file_path_2 = here("projects/leah/_data/private-operators.csv")
df2 = pd.read_csv(file_path_2, sep=',')  

# removing the commas and making the column numeric 
df2["Cameras"] = pd.to_numeric(df2["Cameras"].str.replace(",", ""))
# same as above, sort the states in to descending order based on the flock camera number  
sort = df2.sort_values(by=["Cameras"], ascending=False)

print(sort.head(5))

```

The most popular places for a Flock Camera are Lowe's and The Home Depot by a landslide. What is happening at those stores that is requiring that much surveilance? Looking at the where column, I can see that the majoirty for both Lowe's and The Home Depot are in California. This is very intreging to me as California has the most cameras installed. I want to see where within California the cameras are concentrated. I am going to look deeper into California.

## Third Question: Cities in California and political party?
```{python}
file_path_cities = here("projects/leah/_data/findingflock-cameras-by-city.csv")
```

## Fourth Question: Immigration?
```{python}
file_path_immigration = here("projects/leah/_data/mpi-data-hub_immigrants_n-percent-us-population-by-state-2024.csv")
df_immigration = pd.read_csv(file_path_immigration, sep=',')  
# accidentally had 6000 extra empty lines from the excel file that I downloaded whoops!
df_immigration = df_immigration.drop(df_immigration.index[52:6225])

top_states = df_immigration.loc[df_immigration['State'].isin(['California','Texas', 'Florida', 'Georgia', 'Illinois' ])]
print(top_states)
print(df_immigration)
```

I want to be able to compare these reults with something so I am going to find the average Immigrant Share of Total State Population for all 50 states. There is a row for the whole United States already but I want the average of all individual states in 2024. 

```{python}
#i have to make the column numeric and take away the percent
avg_immigration = df_immigration['Immigrant Share of Total State Population24'].str[:-1].astype(float)
print(avg_immigration)

```

```{python}
# I also have to take away the first row because that represents the entire United States
avg_immigration = avg_immigration.iloc[1:]
print(avg_immigration)

# now I can find the average of the 50 states plus DC
print(avg_immigration.mean())
```

After this calculation, I have found out that the national average percentage of the state population being immigrants is roughly 10.41%. Referring back to the top five states, all five of them had an immigrant share of total state population above 10.41%, with California being almost tripple with a share of 27.6%. Texas has a share of 23.1% which is over double the average. I do not believe this is a coincidence espceially since a common place to find work for undocumented people is the parking lots of The Home Depot and Lowe's. People will crowd around and wait for people to come pick up supplies and ask if they have any work they need done. I will be exploring this further in this next stage.
